outcome: No progress on the mathematical question itself was found since 26 January 2024: the existence of a coprime (gcd=1) amicable pair remains unknown. Two pieces of activity touch the problem without changing it: (1) a February 2026 GitHub issue/PR in DeepMind's formal-conjectures repository formalizes the question as an open Lean statement (not a proof either way), with the Lean formalization itself assisted by an AI model; (2) a January 2026 arXiv paper formalizing amicable-number theory in Lean cites the same >10^65 computational non-existence bound without improving it or resolving the question.
summary: This is the general existence question 'are there any coprime amicable pairs?', which the frozen Wikipedia revision already stated as open with a computational lower bound (then >10^67 on the product; the current article states the same). Searching turned up two items of activity in the window, neither of which changes the mathematics: (1) GitHub issue #2244 in google-deepmind/formal-conjectures (opened 2026-02-10, closed via PR #3531) formalizes the question 'do there exist an amicable pair (a,b) with gcd(a,b)=1?' as a Lean conjecture statement — i.e. it states the open question in a proof assistant, it does not prove or disprove it. The PR's commit message says 'Formalization assisted by Claude Opus 4.6', but per the deep-dive rules a formalisation-only AI contribution is coded ai_role=none regardless of which model helped write the Lean statement, since no mathematics entered the result — the conjecture is still open before and after. (2) The January 2026 arXiv paper 'Formalization of Amicable Numbers Theory' (arXiv:2601.07444) also formalizes classical amicable-number results in Lean 4 and, in the course of that framework, restates the empirical computational bound (searches have found no coprime amicable pair below roughly 10^65) without proving non-existence or finding a coprime pair. Per section 3.1, an infinitude/existence question is only advanced by an answer, and neither item answers it — they restate and formalize the same open question the frozen revision already recorded. Wikipedia's live 'Amicable numbers' article, checked directly, still states 'It is not known whether a pair of coprime amicable numbers exists' with no citation newer than 1969-1970 Hagis papers. I therefore classify this as status=open with no_change_found=true. This aligns with the triage's 'none' verdict; I did not disagree with it, though I went further by opening the actual GitHub issue/PR and arXiv paper rather than just search snippets, and confirmed the AI-assistance detail (Claude Opus 4.6 assisting the Lean formalization) that the triage pass did not surface.
competing_reading: One could argue the DeepMind formal-conjectures repository activity constitutes a form of 'progress' in the broad sense that the conjecture is now machine-formalized and thus more tractable for future automated theorem-proving attempts. But per the rubric, a bare Lean statement of an already-known-open question, with no proof attempt or bound movement, is not a change to the problem's status — it would need to actually attempt or claim a proof to register as `claimed` or `progress`. I also considered whether the AI-assisted formalization should count as `ai_role: assisted`, but the rules explicitly carve out formalisation-only contributions as `none`, so I coded it that way despite the presence of a named, quotable AI system.
what_would_settle_it: Either an exhibited coprime amicable pair (settling it in the affirmative, likely via massive computational search or a novel construction) or a proof that gcd(a,b)=1 is impossible for an amicable pair (settling it in the negative). Short of that, a published improvement to the >10^65 (or >10^67 on the product) search bound would count as `progress`.
